notes: The piezo disc uses the catalogue 'buzzer' type (ports 1/2). Port 1 is the black-wire (ground) side and port 2 is the red-wire (A0) side.
The 'solid surface' in the hardware list is not an electronic part and is not modelled.

In the image the upper half of the breadboard is labelled rows j-f, so it maps to catalogue bank 'b' (rows f-j). Columns 5 and 8 are read from the image: the piezo legs are in 5b.i and 8b.i, and the 1 MΩ resistor is in row h across columns 5 and 8, in parallel with the piezo.

The black wire runs from the Uno GND pin next to AREF (GND.1) to 5b.g, which is in the same strip as the piezo's ground leg and one resistor leg. The red wire runs from A0 to 8b.f, which is in the same strip as the piezo's other leg and the other resistor leg.

The 5V pin in the schematic is only drawn as a supply stub and nothing is connected to it, so there is no 5V connection. Resistor legs are interchangeable, so which leg goes in which column is arbitrary.
No USB cable is listed in the parts, so none is added.
